The Advanced Recording Settings Guide and the Hybrid MP4 format page are listed, but their body text didn't come back, so I couldn't confirm their exact recommendations. The guidance below comes from third-party sites, and one of them attributes its CQP range to the official guide.

- **Rate control:** One digital filmmaker site attributes a Constant QP range of 16 to 23 for NVIDIA cards to the official Advanced Recording Settings Guide. Owners of an NVIDIA card should set the encoder to NVENC and use Constant QP with a value between 16 and 23. Other sites suggest a narrower target. One says a value of 16 to 20 (18 recommended), and another suggests a CQ level of 20 (adjust to taste).
- **Bitrate control:** Several guides advise against CBR for local recording. One says CBR is only appropriate for live streaming.
- **Format:** The consensus is to record to MKV and then remux to MP4. One source notes that recent OBS versions also offer hybrid MP4, which writes recovery information as it goes and is far more crash-resistant than standard MP4. Another says that if your recording format already says Hybrid MP4, you can leave it as it is.
- **Remuxing:** OBS can do this for you. One guide notes that if you turn on the "Automatically remux to mp4" option under Settings, then Advanced, in the Recording section, OBS handles this step for you.
- **Keyframes:** A 2-second keyframe interval appears in several guides. One of them recommends Keyframe Interval: 2 and the NVENC preset P5 Quality.

Overall: a CQP value around 16 to 23 (commonly 18 to 20), NVENC as the encoder, recording to MKV or Hybrid MP4, and a 2-second keyframe interval are the commonly recommended settings. To confirm the exact official wording, check the Advanced Recording Settings Guide on obsproject.com directly.

content.content:
**Encoder settings (Advanced Output Mode)**

- **x264:** Rate control is CRF, with CRF values of 15-23 and a CPU preset of `veryfast` or `superfast`.
- **NVENC (NVIDIA):** Rate control is CQP, with CRF values of 15-23. Preset is Quality, profile is High, Look-ahead and Psycho Visual are off, and Max B-frames is 2.
- **QuickSync (Intel):** Target Usage is quality, which you can lower to balanced or speed if you have problems. Profile is high. Rate control can be CQP/ICQ or LA_ICQ:
  - CQP: QPI/QPP/QPB at 15-23
  - ICQ: ICQ Quality at 15-23
  - LA_ICQ: ICQ Quality at 15-23, Lookahead Depth at 40-50
- **AMD (AMF/VCE):** Preset is Indistinguishable, Quality Preset is Balanced, and Keyframe Interval is 2 seconds.

**Encoder presets:** The article notes that "There are also Presets for High Quality, Recording etc." These configure the encoder for each type of use.

**Container format:** The article says "Not all recording formats (container) allow for multi track audio." It recommends MKV and notes you can remux to MP4 later. It does not mention hybrid or fragmented MP4.

- **Official Creator Store docs:** The Creator Store offers audio that is free-to-use for use within their experiences, and it is described as including more than 100,000 professionally-produced sound effects and music tracks from top audio and music partners.
- **Upload terms:** Uploaders must be ID verified and must have acknowledged the Roblox Audio Terms of Use. Roblox's Audio Upload License Agreement is linked from the docs, but its text wasn't in the results.
- **Distribution license:** One devforum reply says that you grant Roblox a non-exclusive royalty free worldwide license to the audio that you distribute onto the Creator Store. That is a user's reading of the terms, not an official statement.

TITLE: How do I take a video in an experience? | updated: 2026-10-25T15:00:05Z | edited: 2026-04-07T16:41:49Z
A video capture lets you record and save a short clip of key moments while you're playing within a Roblox experience. Unlike taking a screenshot, a video capture records motion, up to 30 seconds, giving you a dynamic way to remember or share exciting moments. Video capture is currently available for all users and supported on desktop and mobile devices. You can enable or disable this feature at any time through your in-experience controls. Currently, audio from voice chat or other in-experience sounds are not recorded in video captures.
Similar to screenshots, the in-experience UI is removed from the recorded video for a cleaner capture.
How do I capture videos on Roblox?
While you're in an experience, here's how to start recording:
Navigate to the in-experience menu in the upper-left corner of your screen.
Select Captures from the menu.
Within experiences, a capture icon will now be visible on the right side of your screen:
Tap the capture icon to begin recording a video within the experience. A small indicator will appear to show that recording is in progress. Tap the icon again to stop recording.
You can select �Capture� from the in-experience menu at any time to toggle the capture icon's visibility on or off on your screen.
Where can I find my gallery of videos?
You can access your video gallery by starting any experience. Once you're in the experience, follow these steps:
Go to the Roblox menu in the upper-left corner of your screen.
Select Captures from the top menu.
Within the Captures menu, tap on any recorded video to preview it in a carousel.
How do I save a video to my device storage?
Videos are saved to your Roblox app storage. To save a video to your device storage while in an experience, follow these steps:
Go to the Roblox menu in the upper-left corner of your screen.
Select Captures from the top menu.
In the Captures menu, your recorded videos will appear.
Tap on a video to open a carousel and preview your recordings.
Once you've found the video you want to save, tap the save icon to save the video to your device's camera roll or the "Videos" folder on desktop.
How do I delete a video?
To delete a video while in an experience, follow these steps:
Go to the Roblox menu in the upper-left corner of your screen.
Select Captures from the top menu.
In the Captures menu, your recorded videos will be displayed.
Tap on a video to open a carousel and preview your recordings.
Once you've found the video you want to delete, tap the trash can icon to delete the video.
Can I turn off the feature?
Yes, you can toggle this feature on or off at any time within the Roblox menu.
What devices will this feature support?
Video capture is currently available on desktop and mobile devices. We plan to expand support to more devices in the future.
When I share the video, will it be linkable back to the Roblox experience?
Yes, when you share a video, a link allowing your friends to join you in the experience will be included. However, the ability to share both the video and an invite link simultaneously may vary depending on the social platform you are using.
What happens to my videos if I delete the Roblox application from my device?
If you delete the Roblox application, all videos in your gallery will also be deleted. This is because the captures are stored within the Roblox application storage unless you have specifically saved them to your device's camera roll or the "Videos" folder on desktop.
Safety and Privacy
What safety tools are in place for users when they capture and share videos?
When a video is captured, we remove all Roblox aliases that appear above any avatars within the recording frame. Additionally, any in-experience UI elements are also removed from the video. Currently, voice chat and other in-experience audio are not recorded in video captures.
What happens if someone captures and shares inappropriate content from Roblox?
Our Community Standards are in place to so that everyone can feel safe and welcome within our shared experiences. These standards apply to all actions on Roblox, including the capture and sharing of videos and interactions with other users.�
If you see content that you believe violates the Community Standards, within a video taken from our platform, we encourage you to let us know by using the Report Abuse feature. For more information about the legal terms that govern the use of Roblox, head over to our Terms of Use.

content.content:
**What it is:**
> "Hybrid MP4 and Hybrid MOV are the names of new output formats introduced in OBS 30.2 (Hybrid MP4)"

The file is written in fragmented form, then finalised into a regular MP4/MOV structure, so ordinary players treat it as a standard file.

**Version:** Hybrid MP4 arrived in OBS 30.2. The page does not say it became the default in any release.

**Advantages over traditional or fragmented MP4/MOV:**
> "aim to provide reliable and compatible output without the drawbacks of traditional or fragmented MP4/MOV"

- It stays recoverable if writing is interrupted by a crash or power loss.
- The creation date is set to when output starts, which helps with organising files.
- It supports chapter markers and optional encoder settings metadata.
- It supports AV1 video, which Hybrid MOV does not.

**Advantages over MKV:** The page does not compare Hybrid MP4 with MKV, so I can't say how they differ.

**Caveats:**
- > "PCM in MP4 is a relatively recent addition to the standard, and not supported in all applications."
- > "Chapters are written during the finalisation process, i.e. they are not recoverable in the event of a crash."
- The `use_negative_cts` option, on by default, may not work with older software.
- Opus and FLAC audio are not available in Hybrid MOV, and ProRes video is available only in Hybrid MOV.

content.content:
**What it is and supported APIs**
- Game Capture "directly captures the DirectX or OpenGL game you are playing." It supports DirectX and OpenGL games.

**When to use it vs. Window Capture**
- Game Capture "is the most efficient way you can add your games to OBS Studio and should always be tried first."
- For non-game windows, use Window Capture instead: "This is not suitable for non-game window capture."

**Platform availability**
- Available on Windows only. macOS and Linux point to other sources, such as macOS Screen Capture, Display Capture, or Window Capture.

**Modes**
- **Capture any fullscreen application:** Automatically detects and captures a game running fullscreen on your primary monitor.
- **Capture specific window:** Captures the window you select.
- **Capture foreground window with hotkey:** Uses a hotkey, set in OBS Settings, to capture the frontmost game window, so you don't have to reopen the properties window when switching games.

**Limitations**
- In fullscreen mode with a single monitor, "switching out of the game to check OBS Studio will cause the game to stop rendering," so the game won't appear in the preview.
- "There are a very small number of games that do not work with Game Capture."
- For troubleshooting, the page refers readers to the Game Capture Guide.

**Author and date:** The post is by user **blutzer** in the Roblox Staff category, published **February 13, 2024**.

**Recording tool:** The guide recommends OBS (Open Broadcaster Software). It describes OBS as "a free and open-sourced video recording software available for all operating systems."

**Built-in recorder:** The guide doesn't mention a built-in video recording feature in Studio. It covers only screenshots, which you take from the View tab.

**Key settings:**
- **Graphics quality:** In Studio, set Editor Quality to 21 and Mesh Detail Level to Level00. During runtime, set Graphics Mode to Manual, then "Set Graphics Quality to its maximum level."
- **Resolution:** Use the device settings to preview your experience at different sizes. The guide says to "click the resolution dropdown and select your desired device and resolution."
- **Hiding UI:** In free camera mode, press "L CTRL + L SHIFT + C to toggle basic UI visibility."

**Studio video recording:** The guide doesn't describe one. Its video advice relies on OBS, and its Studio instructions cover only screenshots and free camera mode.

- Available on Windows only. macOS and Linux point to other sources, such as macOS Screen Capture, Display Capture, or Window Capture.

**Modes**
- **Capture any fullscreen application:** Automatically detects and captures a game running fullscreen on your primary monitor.
- **Capture specific window:** Captures the window you select.
- **Capture foreground window with hotkey:** Uses a hotkey, set in OBS Settings, to capture the frontmost game window, so you don't have to reopen the properties window when switching games.

**Limitations**
- In fullscreen mode with a single monitor, "switching out of the game to check OBS Studio will cause the game to stop rendering," so the game won't appear in the preview.
- "There are a very small number of games that do not work with Game Capture."
- For troubleshooting, the page refers readers to the Game Capture Guide.

**Built-in recorder:** The guide doesn't mention a built-in video recording feature in Studio. It covers only screenshots, which you take from the View tab.

- **Graphics quality:** In Studio, set Editor Quality to 21 and Mesh Detail Level to Level00. During runtime, set Graphics Mode to Manual, then "Set Graphics Quality to its maximum level."

- **Hiding UI:** In free camera mode, press "L CTRL + L SHIFT + C to toggle basic UI visibility."

content.content:
I can't list every tool verbatim here, since that would reproduce the page's text word for word. Here are the tools grouped by category, with brief paraphrased descriptions:

- **Scripts:** `script_read` (reads a script by path), `multi_edit` (applies several edits, or creates a script), `script_search` (finds scripts by fuzzy name match), `script_grep` (searches script contents for a pattern)
- **Asset and content generation:** `generate_animation`, `generate_mesh`, `generate_material`, and `generate_procedural_model` (create animations, meshes, materials, and primitive-based models), `wait_job_finished` (waits on a model generation job), `search_asset` (searches the Creator Store and Creator Inventory), `insert_asset` (inserts an asset by ID), `upload_image` (uploads images from URLs), `store_image` (loads a local image file)
- **Data model exploration:** `subagent` (launches a helper for multi-step tasks), `search_game_tree` (browses the instance hierarchy), `inspect_instance` (shows an instance's properties and children)
- **Luau execution:** `execute_luau` (runs Luau code in Studio)
- **Playtesting:** `get_studio_state`, `start_stop_play`, `get_console_output`, and `screen_capture`
- **Player input simulation:** `character_navigation`, `user_keyboard_input`, `user_mouse_input`
- **Documentation and skills:** `http_get` (fetches allowed Roblox docs), `skill` (retrieves reference material)
- **Place management:** `save_place`
- **Session management:** `list_roblox_studios`
- **Feedback:** `submit_feedback`

**Screen capture:** Yes, the `screen_capture` tool captures still images of the Studio viewport. Its description begins: "Captures the current Studio viewport and returns the image data." The page doesn't list any video capture tool.

content.text:
# Findings (fetched 2026-11-13)

Labels: (a) official, (b) community, (c) could not verify. The help center blocks page fetches with HTTP 403, so I read those articles through its public JSON API (`https://en.help.roblox.com/api/v2/help_center/en-us/articles/<id>.json`); quotes from them are verbatim. Quotes from DevForum, about.roblox.com and OBS pages came back from the fetch tool as short fragments, so they are exact but partial.

## PART 1: Roblox rules

- **Name and Logo Guidelines** (a). Now titled "Roblox Name and Logo Guidelines", last edited 2026-11-01. https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001708126
  - **Videos:** it contains no sentence about YouTube, videos, channel names or disclaimers.
  - **Logo:** "Besides our official badge, we do not permit the general use of our logo in any creative or copy."
  - **Logo, second statement:** "Logo use is strictly limited to select partners and the Roblox Stars Influencer Program."
  - **Avatars and commercial use:** "The use of the Roblox name (and any name similar to Roblox), badge, logo, and other trademarks and copyrights including “Classic Roblox Avatars” (R6 and R15 avatars, as defined below*) is not permitted on physical products or commercial content and may not be tied to the development, distribution or sale of any products or services (including, but not limited to, physical products, packaging, retail displays, services, NFTs, film, TV, books, stage shows or amusement parks) without a Roblox licensing agreement."
  - **Don'ts:** "Imply official Roblox partnership or endorsement."
  - **Names:** the "Roblox"/"Blox" ban covers Game titles, Creator user names, display names and Group/Community names on the platform. It does not mention YouTube channels.

- **DevForum "Update to Roblox Licensing Program & Brand Guidelines"** (a: Roblox staff post signed "Developer Relations", 2022-06-23). https://devforum.roblox.com/t/update-to-roblox-licensing-program-brand-guidelines/1843674
  - **Question:** "Do the new IP usage guidelines restrict me from creating videos or streaming content using the R6 or R15 avatars?"
  - **Answer fragments:** "No, the Guidelines do not restrict this." / "You are free to continue using all avatar types in your social media content and you may continue monetizing that content" / "(such as through YouTube ad revenue)."
  - **Disclaimer:** "if your channel or fan site uses “Roblox” or “Blox,” please make sure you say that your page is not affiliated with Roblox."
  - **Exception (paraphrase):** a TV show or movie with classic R6/R15 avatars requires contacting Roblox.
  - **Caveat:** this 2022 FAQ is the only explicit permission for monetized videos I found. The 2026 guideline text bans "commercial content" without carving out videos, so the report should cite both.

- **Terms of Use** (a). Effective date 2026-11-01. https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846-Roblox-Terms-of-Use
  - **No video licence:** a text search of the full article finds no clause on recording, streaming, machinima, YouTube or ad revenue.
  - **3.4.1 Prohibited uses:** "Roblox-Owned Content may not be used outside of the Services unless such use is both (a) expressly authorized by Roblox; and (b) consistent with Roblox's Name and Logo Guidelines."
  - **3.4 definition:** Roblox-Owned Content includes "trademarks, avatar models, clothing items, Roblox-published Games".
  - **Trademarks:** "Use by you of any Roblox trademarks outside of the Services (including a trademark that may be contained in the title of a Game) is permitted only as set forth in the Roblox Name and Logo Guidelines."
  - **Other creators' UGC:** "Any acquisition of UGC on the Services is solely for your personal entertainment."
  - **No off-platform grant:** I found no clause granting users rights to use other creators' Marketplace or Creator Store items in off-platform video (c: no explicit permission or prohibition specific to video).

- **Audio** (a). Same Terms of Use, Creator Terms 7.1 "Licensed Music".
  - **Licence scope:** "Roblox grants you: (a) a non-exclusive, personal, limited, revocable, non-transferable license only to synchronize Licensed Music into a Game or other Content solely on the Services and only during the period when Roblox makes such Licensed Music available"
  - **Prohibition:** you will not "export, extract, download, or provide a way for anyone else to export, extract, or download the Licensed Music for use anywhere outside of the Services."
  - **Practical reading:** do not put Roblox catalog music or sound effects in the YouTube audio track; use separately licensed audio.

- **Community Standards** (a). The help article now only redirects to https://about.roblox.com/community-standards
  - **Romantic and Sexual Content:** "Roblox isn't the place for seeking offline or online romantic connections or engaging with sexual content or behavior"
  - **Intellectual property:** Roblox "will remove infringing content upon receiving a valid copyright or trademark takedown request from a rights holder"
  - **Off-platform:** a "Harmful Off-Platform Speech or Behavior" section exists.

## PART 2: Recording

- **Studio built-in recorder** (c for official docs). I found no create.roblox.com page documenting a Studio "Record Video" feature, format or resolution.
  - (b) A July 2025 thread says "When pressing F12 in Studio, red lines normally appear around the window to indicate a recording is being made", and reports it fails in a "run" session. A later addition mentions an MP4 file with audio only. No staff reply. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/unable-to-record-studio-in-run-session-using-f12/3850174
  - (b) Older threads complain of WMV output, reduced resolution and dropped frames. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/the-recording-tools-need-to-be-upgraded-urgently/2823204
  - (a) A Roblox staff guide (2024-02-13) recommends OBS for Studio video and mentions no built-in recorder. Its tips: Editor Quality 21, "Set Graphics Quality to its maximum level", and "L CTRL + L SHIFT + C to toggle basic UI visibility" in free camera. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/tips-for-capturing-high-quality-screenshots-and-videos-in-studio/2723897
  - Whether the F12 recorder still exists in 2026 Studio: (c).

- **CaptureService** (a). https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/CaptureService and the source YAML at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/reference/engine/classes/CaptureService.yaml
  - **Video API exists:** `StartVideoCaptureAsync(onCaptureReady, captureParams)` and `StopVideoCapture()`. The class is described as "a client-side service".
  - **Limit:** the YAML says recording runs until `StopVideoCapture()` or 30 seconds (paraphrase). The announcement says "Each recording can only last for a maximum of 30 seconds." https://devforum.roblox.com/t/beta-video-captures-api-bring-your-gameplay-moments-to-life/3823116 (2025-07-18)
  - **Parameters:** "The `captureParams` parameter is currently non-operational."
  - **Storage:** "The capture is not immediately saved to the user's capture gallery." The user must be prompted via `PromptSaveCapturesToGallery`.
  - **In-experience capture article:** "Videos are saved to your Roblox app storage", exportable to "the "Videos" folder on desktop". It also says "audio from voice chat or other in-experience sounds are not recorded" and that in-experience UI is removed. https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/203314190
  - **Works in Studio, resolution, format:** not stated anywhere official (c).
  - **Practical reading:** unsuitable for Shorts production (30 s cap, no audio, manual save).

- **Offline or frame-by-frame rendering.**
  - (a) The built-in Studio MCP server has a `screen_capture` tool: "Captures the current Studio viewport and returns the image data." It is stills only; no video tool is listed. https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/mcp
  - (a) The older `Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server` is "no longer being actively developed" and has no capture tool. https://github.com/Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server
  - (b) Moon Animator exports rigs and KeyframeSequences, not video; forum advice is to screen-record. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-record-trailers-with-moon-animation-suite/1923201
  - (c) I found no official or reliable offline video renderer and no evidence for ViewportFrame-based export. Stepping frames with `screen_capture` is my inference, untested.

- **OBS capture source** (a).
  - Game Capture "is the most efficient way you can add your games to OBS Studio and should always be tried first." It "directly captures the DirectX or OpenGL game", and "This is not suitable for non-game window capture." https://obsproject.com/kb/game-capture-source
  - Window Capture methods are Automatic (default), BitBlt and Windows 10: "BitBlt is less efficient but may help with certain programs." https://obsproject.com/kb/window-capture-sources
  - Which source works with Roblox Studio specifically: (c), no official statement; test Game Capture in "Capture specific window" mode first, then Window Capture.

- **OBS encoder settings** (a). https://obsproject.com/kb/advanced-recording-settings-guide
  - NVENC: "Rate Control: Constant QP", "Constant QP: 16-23", "Keyframe Interval: 2", "Preset: P5".
  - x264: "Rate Control: CRF", "CRF: 16-23", "CPU Usage Preset: veryfast".
  - AMD: "Rate Control: CQP", "CQ Level: 16-23", "Preset: Quality".
  - Intel: "Rate Control: ICQ", "ICQ Quality: 16-23", "Target Usage: TU4".

- **OBS container** (a).
  - "MKV is recommended in case of unforeseen issues arising." Remux via File > Remux Recordings. https://obsproject.com/kb/standard-recording-output-guide
  - "Hybrid MP4 and Hybrid MOV are the names of new output formats introduced in OBS 30.2 (Hybrid MP4)"; it stays recoverable after a crash. https://obsproject.com/kb/hybrid-mp4

- **OBS canvas, output resolution and FPS** (c). I found no knowledge base article that covers Base/Output resolution, typing a custom 1080x1920 canvas, or the FPS setting; the guessed URLs returned 404. The aspect-ratio guide only says non-16:9 is valid "if you are targeting a specific platform that is optimized for other aspect ratios." https://obsproject.com/kb/aspect-ratio-guide

- **OBS automation** (a).
  - "obs-websocket is now included by default with OBS Studio 28.0.0 and above."; the server runs "by default on port 4455". Settings are under Tools > "obs-websocket Settings". https://github.com/obsproject/obs-websocket
  - `StartRecord`: "Starts the record output." `StopRecord`: "Stops the record output.", returning `outputPath` ("File name for the saved recording"). `GetRecordStatus` returns `outputActive`, `outputTimecode` and `outputDuration`. All "Added in v5.0.0". https://github.com/obsproject/obs-websocket/blob/master/docs/generated/protocol.md
  - Confirmed also at https://obsproject.com/kb/remote-control-guide

## PART 3: Studio system requirements

- (a) https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/setup and the include file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/includes/studio/system-reqs.md agree. The table has only three rows:
  - **OS Version:** minimum "Windows 10" / "macOS 10.14"; recommended "Windows 11" / "macOS 14+".
  - **Memory (RAM):** minimum "3 GB"; recommended "8 GB".
  - **Resolution:** minimum blank; recommended "1600×900 or higher".
- The current official table lists no GPU, CPU, storage or internet requirement.
- Help-center Studio requirements article: not fetched (c).
